# Bloom Taxonomy How to Master Any Subject

The video explains Bloom's taxonomy with the example of learning how to make handmade bread. It goes up the six levels, remembering to create, and shows that just decorating and following recipes is not real domain.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on September 3, 2026 (1 min 26 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rDtD-adNluE

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## The pyramid of learning

Bloom's taxonomy explains how you even master a subject. According to the video, most people stop at the decoroba and never really learn [00:00]. The example is learning to make handmade bread from scratch [00:00].

The levels, from base to top [00:00]:

1. Remember: decorate the basic ingredients such as flour, water, salt and yeast [00:00].
2. Understand: understand, superficially, that the mass needs to grow [00:22].
3. Apply: follow a recipe, step by step [00:22].
4. Analyze: when the bread does not grow on a cold day, dismantle the problem and realize that the temperature has stopped the yeast [00:42].
5. Evaluate: judge which variable to change in the next test [00:42].
6. Create: master the principles and no longer depend on a manual [01:03].

## From manual to own recipe

Following instructions without understanding is not domain [00:42]. At the top, the bread that began as a decorated list of ingredients becomes a recipe of its own, because the person internalized the principles of the dough [01:03].

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Bloom's taxonomy?

It is a pyramid of learning levels, which will remember until it creates [00:00].

### Why isn't following a recipe enough?

Because when the recipe fails, only those who analyze and evaluate the problem can correct it. Following instructions without understanding is not domain [00:42].
